name: Training the Beast
summary: In Durotar, young orc and troll hunters are sent to learn from veteran master hunter Ormak Grimshot. After proving themselves with the plains beasts, they travel from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. There they learn to care for, feed, and train a lifelong animal companion.

sections.title: A Journey Beyond the Wilderness
sections.body: In Durotar's arid canyon lands, skill with a bow and survival in the harsh wilds are only part of a hunter's duty. Young hunters first tame the plains beasts: fierce boars, crab scavengers, and armored scorpid stalkers. Once they prove their resilience, Thotar sends them from Razor Hill north through the red clay gulches to Orgrimmar's fortified gates, ready to take responsibility for a companion.

sections.title: The Valley of Honor
sections.body: Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor is an enclave where veteran stalkers and warriors hone their craft. There, aspiring hunters seek Ormak Grimshot, one of the Horde's revered master hunters. He looks beyond their youth to judge whether they have the patience to command a beast and sustain and nurture it through famine, battle, and loss.

sections.title: Bonding with the Wild
sections.body: A beast won through force remains wild until hunter and companion come to understand one another. Ormak teaches the sacred traditions that keep their bond: which foods nourish each creature's spirit, how discipline teaches a beast lethal techniques, and the spiritual focus needed to revive one that falls in the line of duty.

faq.q: Who starts the quest Training the Beast?
aliases: where to start training the beast
faq.answer: Thotar, the hunter trainer outside the barracks in Razor Hill, offers this training after you subdue all three test creatures across Durotar.

faq.q: Where can I find Ormak Grimshot?
faq.answer: Ormak Grimshot is in the Valley of Honor, an eastern district of Orgrimmar, among veteran hunter and warrior mentors.

faq.q: What skills does Ormak Grimshot teach you?
faq.answer: Ormak teaches you to train your companion with active and passive abilities, feed your pet to keep it loyal and content, and revive it if it dies in combat.

faq.q: Why do orc and troll hunters have to visit Orgrimmar for this?
faq.answer: Local trainers like Thotar teach basic wilderness survival. The Horde's elder scouts and venerated trackers, including Ormak Grimshot, preserve advanced beast mastery in the capital.

faq.q: Do other Horde races undertake this exact quest?
faq.answer: No. Orc and troll hunters starting in Durotar undertake this rite. Tauren hunters follow a parallel ritual in Mulgore under their own tribal masters.

faq.q: What happens if a hunter neglects to complete this training?
aliases: do i need to do this
can i skip training the beast
faq.answer: Without this training, a hunter cannot feed, properly train, or resurrect a companion. A captured beast grows unhappy and weak, and is ultimately prone to abandoning its hunter.

angles.text: For a hunter, this training makes your pet a permanent, dependable ally rather than a fleeting summon, and teaches you the arts of Feed Pet and Revive Pet.
Orcs regard the bond with a hunting companion as a matter of martial honor and duty, tested in battle across Durotar's harsh frontiers.
For Darkspear trolls making a new home in Kalimdor, learning to commune with Durotar's savage creatures is vital to scouting and surviving on unfamiliar soil.
The Horde relies on scouts and beasts to secure Durotar's and the Barrens' fragile borders against centaur, quilboar, and Alliance incursions.
